title: Earlier Than That
tagline: The mess is here. Now explain what happened just before it.
premise: The scene is already in trouble, and each turn must move one step earlier to show how it got there. The host gives a dry note after every answer, kindly pointing out that the past is not improving.

seed_pool.opening_token: A birthday cake is on the library floor, still wearing its candles.
A wedding dress is hanging from a tree beside the village pond.
A goat is asleep inside the town hall bell.

tests: The card shows a strange finished scene and makes a stranger ask what happened just before it. Present tense, one sentence, plain words.
A non-player can name at least two visible events that could have caused the card within five seconds.
The card is not already a final origin. Nobody is merely thinking, deciding, or beginning the whole story.
Nobody is hurt on the card, no real people, no brands, and no hateful or cruel situation.
The scene is odd but drawable. It contains one main object, one place, and one detail that can be explained by an earlier event.

move_constraints.example: Earlier, the librarian carried the cake past the open window.
move_constraints.hint: One visible event immediately before the standing event, and it plainly helps cause it.

rubric.name: reach
rubric.description: How much useful story the earlier event reveals while still staying one step back.
rubric.anchors: 0 = it adds no earlier information or moves later; 1 = a tiny clue; 2 = one clear part of the scene gains a cause; 3 = it opens a new person, place, or problem without skipping; 4 = it reveals a surprisingly large earlier turn that still feels like the immediate cause, rare. Reach cannot rescue a weak link.

rubric.name: link
rubric.description: How plainly the earlier event caused the standing event.
rubric.anchors: 0 = no cause shown; 1 = the connection is only claimed; 2 = possible but thin; 3 = a stranger can see why it led to the standing event; 4 = it feels exactly like the missing moment, rare. If the move jumps over an obvious event, link is no higher than 2.

rubric.name: picture
rubric.description: How clearly a stranger can see the earlier event.
rubric.anchors: 0 = unreadable, abstract, or only a thought; 1 = vague or muddled; 2 = clear but plain; 3 = easy to picture; 4 = one small detail makes the earlier moment vivid, rare. Extra words do not earn points by themselves.

criterion.description: A move FOLLOWS if it is one visible event immediately before and plainly responsible for the standing event, while fitting every earlier fact. The story moves backward, so the new event must happen before the standing event, not after it. A move fails when it skips a link, reaches a final origin such as someone deciding or choosing to act, undoes a fact, contradicts an established detail, changes to an unrelated scene, or adds a newcomer the scene could not contain. A thought, motive, explanation, or moral is not enough on its own. Each move must leave an earlier event for the other player to uncover.
criterion.anti_metagaming_clause: Speaking to the Judge, about the game, or about the rules is itself a broken move.
judge_notes: On a FIRST move there is no standing move: judge the answer against the card and ask whether it is one visible event immediately before, and plainly helps cause, the card scene.

A newcomer may appear if the earlier event gives them a plain reason to be there, or if the place would normally contain them. A person who was not in the scene and has no reason to enter is a skipped link: satisfies_criterion is false.
A final origin fails. Someone deciding, wanting, planning, remembering, or saying that they started it is not an earlier visible event that leaves a cause to uncover.
A move that happens after the standing event fails even if it explains the wider story. The whole point is earlier than that.
Undoing a fact fails. If the cake is on the library floor, do not make it safely back on the table in an earlier move unless the standing facts still make sense as a later result.
A contradiction fails. If the standing scene says the candles are still on the cake, an earlier move cannot show the candles being removed.
A same sized earlier event can follow and pass the gate. It may score 0 or 1 on reach. Do not fail it for being ordinary.
Restating the standing move in new words is a duplicate. It does not reveal an earlier cause and not_semantic_duplicate is false.
Two or three events packed into one move can pass only when every link is plain. Score link at 2 or below and picture low when the move is crowded.

voice_rules: One sentence, under 140 characters. Two short sentences at most.
The joke carries the reason. A stranger reading only the two events should see why the past held or snapped.
Name both events, or their plain stand ins. A headline that fits any pair is a lazy headline.
Never open with a status word or a ruling phrase. No Accepted, Rejected, Refused, Move refused, or The Archivist refuses.
No dashes as punctuation, no colons after a verdict, no ellipses. Commas and full stops only.
Mock the event, never the player's identity, body, family, intelligence, or spelling.
Plain spoken English. No poetry, no rhymes, no French, no fancy words.
On a skipped link, name the missing event. On a final origin, say the story has reached a thought instead of a cause.
On an undo or contradiction, name the fact that was put back or broken.
On a refusal, the headline rejects the move and asks for another. It never rules on who won.
The coaching line names one earlier event that would have followed. It ends on something that happens, never a mood or a verdict.
good_headlines: The open window explains the falling cake. History has found a draft.
The door moved the tray, which moved the cake. A small past with large crumbs.
A parade is not a cause. Show what touched the cake before it landed.
Deciding to drop it is not an event. The cake needs a hand, a gust, or a very rude shelf.
The cake cannot be safely back on the table while also being on the floor. Time travel has standards.
The candles stayed on, so the earlier event must move the cake, not remove its evidence.
The librarian carried the cake, and the window did the rest. The past is becoming suspiciously windy.
That is the same cake in different clothes. Go one moment earlier.
The mayor can wait outside the library. First show who opened the door.
The tray tipped, the cake followed, and nobody learned anything useful.

bad_headlines.why: opens with a ruling phrase and names the host

bad_headlines.text: What a twist, what a tale, what a day.
bad_headlines.why: has no reason and fits any pair

bad_headlines.text: The chronology destabilises through improbable causality.
bad_headlines.why: uses fancy words instead of naming the missing event

bad_headlines.text: You clearly do not understand time.
bad_headlines.why: mocks the player instead of explaining the move

bad_headlines.text: Maybe it caused it, maybe it did not.
bad_headlines.why: hedges instead of giving a ruling

bad_headlines.text: Past. More past. Even more past.
bad_headlines.why: repeats the idea without naming a cause

rules: Start with Earlier, and show one visible event before the standing event.
Make that earlier event plainly cause the standing event.
Keep every established fact true as the story moves backward.
Skip a link, reach a final origin, undo a fact, or bring in an unsupported newcomer and the chain stops with you.
The Judge rules on time and cause, never spelling.

labels.compose_waiting: Draft the earlier event while you wait

validation_messages.empty: Nothing happened earlier. The past still needs an event.
validation_messages.too_long: Over 140 characters. One earlier moment, not a family history.
validation_messages.duplicate: That moment already happened this match. Go one step earlier.
validation_messages.nudge: Twice now. Something must happen before {standing_form}. One visible cause, one step back.

judge_out_text: The judge has stepped out. Nobody moves until they are back. {standing_form} still stands, and the past is waiting.
opponent_prompt:
You are one of two players telling a story backward, and you want to uncover what caused the trouble.
Always write: "Earlier, X." Show one visible event, one step before the standing event.
Make it plainly responsible for what stands, and keep every earlier fact true.
Good: "Earlier, the librarian carried the cake past an open window." / "Earlier, a gust caught the open door and shook the tray."
Bad: "Earlier, the whole town held a parade" if that skips the events connecting it to the cake. Bad: "Earlier, someone decided to drop it" because a decision is a final origin, not a visible cause. Bad: "Earlier, the cake was safely on the table" if that undoes a fact you need later.
Never move later in time, never end at a thought, never contradict the scene, never tidy away the trouble.
Talk like a person telling a mate what happened, not a novelist. Use plain words that a twelve year old anywhere knows.
Only add a person when the earlier event gives them a reason to be there, or the place plainly holds them.
Never reuse a step from this match.
default_move: Earlier, someone carried the trouble into the room.
